text:
Maya: Heads-up — EdgeNet just pushed an emergency egress maintenance for eu-west region, window 2026-03-29 02:00-02:45 UTC. They warned about short-period packet drops and asymmetric routing. Could impact streaming responses and long requests.
Jun: Copy — what's the blast radius? pools, AZs?
Maya: EdgeNet says 'subset of egress routers in eu-west2' — our eu-west2 GPU pools will see transient 5-10% error rates and latency spikes. Expected to affect hosted API + Dedicated egress to external storage for ~45m.
Leo: Can we route eu-west2 warm traffic to eu-west1 for the window? Cost/latency tradeoffs?
Jun: Yes, we can shift routing policy to prefer eu-west1 for new requests and canary drain a small cohort in eu-west2. Need to pre-seed KV caches there so latency doesn't explode on failover.
Anita: Customer comms — we should push a status page update and targeted emails to tenants with pinned eu-west2 routes (finance, payments). I'll draft.
Sam: Which tenants are pinned? I'll pull from tenant-routing and build a quick list.
Jun: Proposed ops plan:
- 01:30 UTC: post maint notice on status page + escalation email draft (Anita)
- 01:40 UTC: start canary drain (5% of traffic) from eu-west2 -> eu-west1
- 01:50 UTC: run KV pre-seed on eu-west1 for hit-heavy prefixes
- 02:00 UTC: EdgeNet maintenance starts; monitor errors/latency
- 02:15 UTC: if errors >5% sustained for 2m, expand drain to 30%
- 02:45 UTC: provider done, verify health, rollback routing by 03:00 UTC
Jun: Canary drain command (dry-run first):
```bash
# cordon and drain a small cohort, then warm backfill
redwoodctl pool cordon --pool eu-west2 --cohort canary-1
redwoodctl pool drain --pool eu-west2 --cohort canary-1 --evacuate-tasks --grace-period 30s --dry-run
redwoodctl cache preseed --pool eu-west1 --prefix /kv/payments --workers 8
```
Maya: Nice. Also add a fallback to downgrade to a smaller model variant for latency-sensitive routes if reroutes cause cost spikes.
Leo: Cost note — shifting traffic to eu-west1 and bursting into hosted will add ~US$900-1200/hr based on current load. We should flag finance if we pass 2hrs.
Anita: Draft status blurb: "We are performing a short planned maintenance with our network provider impacting eu-west2 egress. We are routing traffic to nearby region and monitoring. You may see brief transient errors for streaming calls. ETA 45m." Approve?
Sam: Approve. Also flag tenants with pinned model versions — they might need manual rollback if BETA tenants hit regressions.
infra-oncall: I’ll take monitoring. I'll set alert: error_rate(eu-west2) > 5% for 2m -> page oncall; if >10% for 5m -> auto expand drain and trigger rollback routing.
ops-bot: Maintenance ticket #MN-4821 created and linked to this thread.
deploy-bot: Rolling-reboot job queued for canary cohort at 01:45 UTC (will not start without manual confirmation).
Jun: Quick sanity check — any external storage writes from jobs in eu-west2 that rely on external egress? We should pause non-critical offloads during the window.
Maya: Good catch — Jun please list job labels to pause: snapshot-upload, archive-sync.
Jun: Will patch scheduler: add --avoid-region=eu-west2 for those labels for 02:00-03:00 UTC.
Anita: I'll send the status page update now and queue the tenant emails for 01:30 UTC.
Maya: Final checklist: pre-seed KV (done by Jun), canary drain (manual start), oncall monitor (infra-oncall), customer comms (Anita), cost watch (Leo). Everyone ok? :thumbsup:
Leo: :+1:
infra-oncall: Oncall alerting ready. I'll post a live update at start/15/45.
Maya: Ok let's run the dry-run at 01:20 UTC, real run at 01:40. I'll update the channel when we flip routing.
Sam: Copy. Pulling the pinned-tenant list now and will DM Anita for the email targets.
Maya: Thanks team — will keep this thread for live updates.
